3                     UNITED STATES DISTRICT COURT                       

4                          DISTRICT OF NEVADA                            

5                                  * * *                                 

6    RICHARD GIBSON, et al.,           Case No. 2:23-cv-00140-MMD-DJA    

7                         Plaintiffs,            ORDER                   
         v.                                                             
8                                                                        
    MGM RESORTS INTERNATIONAL, et                                       
9    al.,                                                                

10                      Defendants.                                      

11                                                                       
   I.   SUMMARY                                                         
12                                                                       
        Plaintiffs Richard Gibson and Heriberto Valiente, on behalf of themselves and all 
13                                                                       
   others similarly situated, allege that defendant hotel operators on the Las Vegas Strip 
14                                                                       
   including Defendant MGM Resorts International unlawfully restrained trade in violation of 
15                                                                       
   Section 1 of the Sherman Antitrust Act, 15 U.S.C. § 1, et seq. (“Sherman Act”) by 
16                                                                       
   artificially inflating the price of hotel rooms after agreeing to all use pricing software 
17                                                                       
   marketed by the same company. (ECF No. 1 (“Complaint”).) Before the Court is MGM’s 
18                                                                       
   motion to dismiss.1 (ECF No. 92 (“Motion”).) As further explained below, because the 
19                                                                       
   Complaint does not contain allegations that any MGM hotels within Plaintiffs’ defined 
20                                                                       
   market area of the Las Vegas Strip use the Rainmaker software, the Court will grant the 
21                                                                       
   Motion.                                                              
22                                                                       
   II.  BACKGROUND                                                      
23                                                                       
        The following allegations are adapted from the Complaint. Plaintiffs “challenge an 
24                                                                       
   unlawful agreement among Defendants to artificially inflate the prices of hotel rooms on 
25                                                                       
   the Las Vegas Strip above competitive levels.” (ECF No. 1 at 3.) The gist of the alleged 
26                                                                       
   conspiracy is that all of the defendant hotel operators agreed to use a shared set of pricing 
27                                                                       
28                                                                       
        1Plaintiffs responded (ECF No. 110), and MGM replied (ECF No. 124). This order 
2   supracompetitive prices to the hotel operators. (Id. at 3.) Plaintiffs define the Las Vegas 
3   Strip as “the four-mile stretch in the unincorporated towns immediately south of the City 
4   of Las Vegas.” (Id. at 3 n.1.) Plaintiffs otherwise explain why the Las Vegas Strip allegedly 
5   constitutes a relevant antitrust market, primarily because it is unique. (Id. at 13-14.) 
6        Plaintiffs define MGM as one of the defendant hotel operators. (Id. at 3 n.2.) MGM 
7   allegedly:                                                           
8        rents hotel rooms in Las Vegas, Nevada at multiple hotel properties. MGM 
         operates the Bellagio, VDARA at Aria, Aria, Park MGM, New York-New 
9        York, MGM Grand, Excalibur, Luxor, Mandalay Bay, and the Four Seasons 
         Hotel. MGM is one of Cendyn’s clients and uses its revenue management 
10        software.                                                       
11   (Id. at 12.) Plaintiffs otherwise allege that MGM ‘controls’ the Cosmopolitan Hotel on the 
12   Las Vegas Strip as well. (Id. at 14.) As to the Cosmopolitan, a confidential witness who is 
13   allegedly a former employee of Cendyn is quoted in the Complaint as saying, “Caesars 
14   probably knew we were in the Cosmopolitan and vice versa.” (Id. at 10.) 
15        Plaintiffs also discuss how an MGM-operated hotel called the Borgata Hotel in 
16   Atlantic City, New Jersey uses Rainmaker’s GuestRev pricing algorithm to validate the 
17   pricing recommendations the pertinent employee makes to her management. (Id. at 17.) 
18   These allegations are drawn from marketing materials on Cendyn’s website. (Id. at 17 n. 
19   19, 20.) Plaintiffs also mention that MGM is one of the two largest players on the Las 
20   Vegas Strip in terms of hotel ownership in describing how the Las Vegas Strip hotel 
21   market is highly concentrated. (Id. at 23.)                          
22        The remainder of Plaintiffs’ allegations in their Complaint discuss either Hotel 
23   Operators or Defendants generally, but not MGM specifically. (See generally id.) MGM 
24   appears to represent in its Motion that none of its hotels on the Las Vegas Strip use any 
25   Rainmaker software when it writes, “Plaintiffs do not, however, and cannot, allege that 
26   any of the ten Las Vegas properties they allege MGM operates uses Rainmaker software 
27   that  provides  them  with  any  pricing  recommendations  or  data.”  (ECF  No.  92  at  4 
28   (emphasis added).)                                                   
2        MGM argues in pertinent part that Plaintiffs’ claims against it should be dismissed 
3   because they fail to allege in their Complaint that MGM uses any Rainmaker software at 
4   any of the ten hotels on the Las Vegas Strip MGM allegedly operates, much less that 
5   these hotels accept all of the recommendations any software provides to them. (Id. at 3.) 
6   Plaintiffs counter that three sets of allegations, taken together, plausibly allege MGM is 
7   part of the alleged conspiracy on the Las Vegas Strip. (ECF No. 110 at 8-10.) The Court 
8   agrees with MGM.                                                     
9        The  United  States  Court  of  Appeals  for  the  Ninth  Circuit  “require[s]  some 
10   showing—direct  or  circumstantial—that  the  [Sherman  Act]  defendants  ‘actively 
11   participated in an individual capacity in the scheme.”’ SmileDirectClub, LLC v. Tippins, 31 
12   F.4th 1110, 1119 (9th Cir. 2022) (citations omitted); see also id. at 1119-20 (affirming 
13   dismissal of certain defendants in Sherman Act case because the complaint pleaded 
14   nothing to implicate them in the alleged conspiracy); see also In re California Bail Bond 
15   Antitrust Litig., 511 F. Supp. 3d 1031, 1047 (N.D. Cal. 2021) (“To survive a motion to 
16   dismiss, a complaint alleging an antitrust conspiracy “must allege that each individual 
17   defendant joined the conspiracy and played some role in it because, at the heart of an 
18   antitrust conspiracy is an agreement and a conscious decision by each defendant to join 
19   it.”) (citation omitted). Indeed, even Plaintiffs argue that they must “make allegations that 
20   plausibly suggest that each [d]efendant participated in the alleged conspiracy.” (ECF No. 
21   110 at 7 (citing In re Static Random Access Memory (SRAM) Antitrust Litig., 580 F. Supp. 
22   2d 896, 903-04 (N.D. Cal. 2008)).)                                   
23        Plaintiffs’ Complaint does not plausibly allege that MGM joined Plaintiffs’ alleged 
24   conspiracy to fix prices on the Las Vegas Strip. The Court addresses each allegation or 
25   set of allegations that Plaintiffs point to in their opposition in turn. 
26        Plaintiffs  first  point  to  their  allegations  (pulled  from  Cendyn’s  own  marketing 
27   materials) that an MGM-operated hotel in Atlantic City, New Jersey, the Borgata Hotel, 
28   uses Rainmaker. (ECF No. 110 at 8-9.) This does not show that MGM-operated hotels 
2   software. Atlantic City is not within the relevant market as Plaintiffs have alleged it. (ECF 
3   No. 1 at 13-14 (defining the Las Vegas Strip as the relevant antitrust market area and 
4   explaining why that specific geography matters so much).) And MGM is a large company 
5   that operates many hotels, so it is not plausible to suggest (especially considering the 
6   dearth of other pertinent factual allegations in the Complaint) that, because one hotel 
7   uses a piece of software, all MGM-operated hotels use it.            
8        Moreover, the Complaint contains the cryptic sentence, “MGM is one of Cendyn’s 
9   clients and uses its revenue management software.” (Id. at 12.) Cendyn presumably has 
10   many products, so saying that MGM is a client does not mean it uses the specific 
11   Rainmaker software central to Plaintiffs’ alleged conspiracy. The same goes for the 
12   related allegation that MGM, “uses its revenue management software.” That does not 
13   necessarily mean Rainmaker, much less the same Rainmaker software as the other hotel 
14   defendants, much less that MGM accepts all of the recommendations it is presented with 
15   by the unspecified software. And there is indeed no dispute that MGM uses revenue 
16   management software, specifically Rainmaker, at a hotel it operates in Atlantic City. So 
17   the statement that MGM uses Cendyn’s revenue management software could very well 
18   mean that it does so only at the Borgata Hotel in Atlantic City. And this statement is 
19   otherwise not inconsistent with what MGM argues in its Motion—that it does not use the 
20   Rainmaker software at any of the 10 or 11 (depending on whether one counts the 
21   Cosmopolitan) hotels mentioned in the Complaint that MGM operates on the Las Vegas 
22   Strip, though it does at the Borgata Hotel.                          
23        Plaintiffs next point to a 2015 press release from Rainmaker stating that MGM is 
24   among its clients, and two statements from confidential witnesses who used to work for 
25   Cendyn that Rainmaker is used by ‘just about every hotel on the Las Vegs Strip’ and a 
26   more specific estimate that Rainmaker is used by ‘90% of the Hotels on the Las Vegas 
27   Strip.’ (ECF No. 110 at 9-10.) But none of these statements establish that the 10 hotels 
28   MGM operates on the Las Vegas Strip (excluding the Cosmopolitan, which the Court 
2   minority of hotels that do not use the Rainmaker software. Plaintiffs simply do not allege 
3   that the 10 MGM-operated hotels on the Las Vegas strip use the Rainmaker software in 
4   a way otherwise contemplated by Plaintiffs’ purported conspiracy. And as to the press 
5   release, that too could just as easily refer to the Borgata Hotel as to any of the many other 
6   hotels MGM operates. These allegations lack the requisite link to MGM-operated hotels 
7   on the Las Vega Strip.                                               
8        Plaintiffs finally point to the Cosmopolitan being touted as a ‘success story’ on 
9   Cendyn’s own website, but concede the video Plaintiffs point to was made in 2019, before 
10   MGM began operating the hotel in 2021. (ECF No. 110 at 10.) The Court also agrees with 
11   MGM that it is notable Plaintiffs do not include the Cosmopolitan in their list of hotels 
12   operated by MGM. (ECF No. 124 at 7.) The plausible inference to draw from that notable 
13   omission is that the time periods do not overlap—that the Cosmopolitan used Rainmaker 
14   before MGM took over its operations. And there are otherwise no allegations in the 
15   Complaint that specifically discuss MGM, as opposed to the hotel operator defendants or 
16   Defendants  generally.  Said  otherwise,  the  Complaint  does  not  contain  allegations 
17   sufficient to plausibly suggest that any MGM hotels within Plaintiffs’ defined market area 
18   of the Las Vegas Strip use the Rainmaker software.                   
19        In sum, the Court will grant the Motion because Plaintiffs do not plausibly allege 
20   that any MGM hotels within Plaintiffs’ defined market of the Las Vegas Strip used the 
21   Rainmaker software in a way otherwise alleged as the alleged conspiracy Plaintiffs 
22   challenge in this case. MGM is accordingly dismissed from this case without prejudice, 
23   as the Court cannot say that amendment would be futile. The allegations that an MGM-
24   operated hotel in  New Jersey  uses  Rainmaker, and the allegations  about  how the 
25   Cosmopolitan at least used to use Rainmaker suggest that it is possible that Plaintiffs 
26   could add further factual allegations to their Complaint to show that MGM participated in 
27   the alleged conspiracy on the Las Vegas Strip. Any amended complaint must be filed 
28   within 30 days of the date of entry of this order.                   
 1  || IV.    CONCLUSION 
2          The Court notes that the parties made several arguments and cited several cases 
3 || not  discussed  above.  The  Court  has  reviewed  these  arguments  and  cases  and 
4 || determines that they do not warrant discussion as they do not affect the outcome of the 
5 || Motion before the Court. 
6          It  is therefore  ordered  that  MGM’s  motion  to  dismiss  (ECF  No.  92)  is  granted. 
7 || Dismissal  is without prejudice and with  leave to  amend.  Specifically,  the Court grants 
8 ||  Plaintiffs leave to file an amended complaint that includes MGM as a defendant if Plaintiffs 
9 || wish to again attempt to allege that MGM participated in the purported conspiracy. Any 
10 || amended  complaint  must  be filed  within  30  days  of the  date  of  entry of this  order.  If 
11  ||  Plaintiffs do not comply with this amendment deadline, the Court may dismiss MGM from 
12 ||  this case, with prejudice, without further advance notice to Plaintiffs. 
13          DATED THIS 24" Day of October 2023. 

15                                             
                                         MIRANDA M. DU 
16                                        CHIEF UNITED STATES DISTRICT JUDGE
